name: Nine-Card Don
description: Nine-Card Don (also known as Big Don or Welsh Don) is a traditional British pub game for four players in fixed partnerships. It is a descendant of the 17th-century game All Fours. Unlike the Irish version, only nine cards are dealt to each player, leaving a significant portion of the deck unseen, which adds a layer of uncertainty and boneyard-tracking to the strategy.
origin: United Kingdom (specifically North West England and South Wales)

history.origins: Don evolved from Dom Pedro in the 19th century. While Ireland developed the 13ndcard version, British players in Cheshire, Lancashire, and South Wales standardized the 9ndcard version.
timeline: 1800s: All Fours variations like Dom Pedro spread through the UK.
Early 20th Century: The 9-card version becomes a staple in industrial pub culture (the 'Black Country' and Welsh mining valleys).
Modern Era: Maintained by dedicated leagues such as the Bolton Don League and the Abercarn Crib & Don League.
history.cultural: Used as a major social catalyst in the British regimental system and workingndclass social clubs.
history.evolution: The game is uniquely characterized by the immediate scoring ('pegging') of fives and trumps during play.

setup.dealing: Each player receives 9 cards (dealt in batches of 3). The remaining 16 cards are set aside and not used in the hand.

rules.objective: Reach 121 points by capturing scoring cards and winning the 'Game' point.
rules.gameplay:
1. The Pitch: The player to the dealer's left leads a card. The suit of this card is the trump suit.
2. Trick Play: Players must follow suit if possible. In strict All Fours tradition, some leagues allow 'playing a trump' even if you have the led suit.
3. Card Ranking: A (high) K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2.
keyRules: Only the 36 dealt cards are scored for the 'Game' point.
Fives are often called 'Don cards' or 'Pedros'.
Winning the 'Low' point requires tracking the lowest trump seen in play.

strategy.basic: Identify the trump suit quickly and secure your 5ndpoint cards (all 5s regardless of suit) as soon as your team wins a trick.
strategy.intermediate: Since 16 cards are missing, do not assume high trumps like the King or Queen are in play. If you hold the Jack, it might be the highest trump.
strategy.advanced: Bidding/Pitching Strategy: Pitch a suit where you hold a 5 to secure immediate points, or pitch a suit where you have a void to allow your partner to trump in.
tips: All 5s are high-value targets. Don't waste them on tricks your partner can't win.
The 'Game' point is decided by the 10s and Aces; try to capture these even if they don't provide immediate pegging points.
